summary.text: Jenny Rae Le Roux, a Republican business owner and management executive, lost the November 3, 2026 election for the U.S. House seat in California's 47th District to Dave Min.
She ran for California governor as a Republican in the 2021 recall election and the 2022 regular election.
She directs CAL DOGE, an initiative tied to Republican statewide candidates, and said her work there led her to run for Congress.

paragraphs.text: Le Roux was born in Memphis, Tennessee. She earned a B.A. in economics from the University of Virginia in 2002 and an M.B.A. from Columbia Business School in 2018.
Her career includes owning a business, serving as managing director of Management Consulted, and working as an author and strategic advisor.
She told Fox News that she had a farm, a family and a business, and that the COVID-19 pandemic led her to become politically active.
Le Roux ran for governor of California as a Republican in the 2021 recall election and again in 2022, finishing fourth in the June 2022 primary with 3.5% of the vote.
She serves as director of CAL DOGE, an initiative launched by Republican gubernatorial candidate Steve Hilton and state controller candidate Herb Morgan.
In the June 2, 2026 top-two primary in the 47th District she took 25.0% of the vote, second to Rep. Dave Min, and she was endorsed in this race by the Republican Party of California.
She received 42.2% of the vote to Dave Min's 57.8%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.

sources.title: Republican cousin of Virginia Gov. Spanberger launches California House bid
